title: Parapet Coping That Leaks
description: A ceiling stain along the outside wall of a Houston shop is often the parapet coping and the wall flashing, not a hole in the middle of the roof.
html:
The stain is at the top of the wall, inside, under the parapet. People look for a hole in the middle of the roof because that is the roof they can imagine. The water is usually coming from the cap on the wall, or from the joint where the membrane turns up and is supposed to end. The field of the roof can be dry.

Coping has to shed back onto the roof

Metal coping is the lid on the parapet. It should slope inward, toward the roof, so rain on the cap falls onto the membrane you can see and maintain. Joints in the coping need a splice that moves with the heat, not a smear of sealant as the only lap. When the slope goes the wrong way, or a joint opens, water enters the top of the wall and shows up inside, sometimes floors below the roof deck.

Below the coping, the membrane should run up the wall and terminate under a bar or a reglet, with counterflashing over it. A termination that has pulled out, or a counterflashing that was never cut into the mortar, lets water behind the membrane. From the roof that looks like a tight wall. From the stockroom it looks like a roof leak. Opening the cap is how you tell.

Masonry has its own path

Brick parapets also leak through the wall itself if the through-wall flashing is missing or clogged with mortar. That is a masonry detail. We can replace coping and reflash the roofing termination. We will not pretend a coating on the field fixes a wall that is wet from the top down. If both are true, we say both.

This is the work on a commercial roof repair, and it is cheaper when the coping is the whole job. If your stain tracks the outside wall, walk us to that wall first. Call (281) 541-0027 or request an inspection.
